text.p: Severe weather with wind damage, flooding rains, hail, and tornadoes raked much of eastern Texas, Arkansas, parts of northern Mississippi and also portions of Tennessee, Kentucky, West Virginia, and southern Ohio on the weekend. The hardest-hit area in terms of tornadoes was Arkansas, with Kentucky getting the brunt of the flooding. More rainfall is expected on Wednesday across the region, hampering cleanup efforts, and possibly leading to additional flooding.

Tropical cyclone Gavin will become strong risk to shipping in the southwest Pacific during the next 48 hours. Winds are currently estimated at 70 mph but they should reach 105-110 mph in 48 hours and 110-115 mph in 72 hours. The system is currently east of the Santa Cruz islands, well north-northwest of Fiji. The system is expected to turn southward during the next 24-48 hours. It will be over open water during this time but this southward turn means that the Fiji islands may be threatened late in the period.
There are no further emergency statements at this time.
